From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Mark Davis <mark.davis@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: traffic-split + rollback lattice for Aug patch sprint

Team —

We need to finalize the maintenance plan for the Aug patch sprint that will touch customer-private fleets (Acme Health staging + prod). High level asks:

- Confirm pinned version semantics for this release (semantic pin vs. exact build)
- Agree traffic-split and canary cadence (percent + duration)
- Define clear rollback lattice + abort criteria (who executes, what triggers immediate rollback)
- Validate network drain and KV cache evacuation steps with Acme SRE

Attached a draft upgrade matrix and a short canary-playbook. I propose the following default plan:

1) Pin config: exact artifact tag (build-2026.08.01) on prod nodes during the window; allow staging to accept semver range for smoke.
2) Canary: 5% traffic, 30 minutes soak, automated health checks (error-rate > 0.5% or p50 latency +30% -> abort).
3) Traffic ladder: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 20–30 min gates.
4) Rollback: immediate full-failback to previous artifact if KV-coherency or persistent 503 seen; otherwise staged rollback by unpinning and forcing old tag for new requests.

Acme: Mark, can you confirm your SRE team can run the network drain steps (attached) and accept a 5% canary during their business hours?

I need signoff by EOD Wed so we can schedule the window for Sun Aug 8 00:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic).

Thanks,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.example.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>

Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: traffic-split + rollback lattice for Aug patch sprint

Mina —

Quick callouts from an ops perspective:

- Pinning: agree with exact artifact tag for prod. We should add an emergency "shelve" flag that prevents any new deploys to a fleet for 24h in case of chain regressions.
- Canary % and gates: 5%/30m looks fine. Add an automated KV-consistency check (script included in canary-playbook.md) to validate cache coherency after each step.
- Network drain: we should ensure host-level connections are drained and also invalidate client-side caches at the CDN edge; Mark please confirm if you can toggle edge TTL for the window.
- Rollback executor: designate on-call infra lead (Jonas) to execute immediate full-failback, and PM (Mina) to coordinate external comms.

I updated the upgrade-matrix with a "shelve-flag" column and a preflight smoke checklist. See attachment.

—Marissa

Folks —

Thanks Mark, that answers the edge question. On the KV divergence: recommend the following escalation ladder (brief):

A) If divergence limited to read-heavy endpoints and cache TTLs are acceptable -> targeted rollback (service subset) + force-repopulate KV for affected keys.
B) If divergence is widespread or affects write paths -> immediate full-fleet rollback to previous artifact + shelve flag.
C) Automated triggers (should force immediate rollback): sustained error-rate > 1% for 5m; p50 latency > 2x baseline for 5m; any data-corrupting exceptions.

Operational notes: I will be on-call for the window and can execute the rollback scripts. Please confirm who will own customer-facing comms if we trigger a full-fleet rollback (Mina?).

Jonas
SRE, Redwood Inference

All —

I pulled together a concise runbook for the window (see canary-playbook.md attached). Key additions:
- Health checks: add an application-level "KV-consistency" probe and a synthetic inference test for 256-token requests; failure of either for 3 consecutive probes -> abort.
- Circuit breaker: if per-node token processing CPU > 85% for 3m -> reduce canary traffic by 50% or pause ladder.
- Observability: ensure dashboards have the previous 24h baseline overlayed and an escalation channel (#prod-private-patching).

I've updated the Confluence page and linked the runbook. If there are no objections I'll mark this plan as ready and request the maintenance window.

—Stephanie
